about: Company car benefit (benefit in kind) for tools/build-company-car-pages.js: HMRC's appropriate percentages by CO2 and electric range, transcribed by script from 480 Appendix 2, and the calculation steps from 480 Chapter 12, each quoted. Add each new tax year's table when HMRC publishes it.

sources.title: Work out the appropriate percentage for company car benefits (480: Appendix 2)
How to work out the benefit of a company car (480: Chapter 12)
Tax on company benefits: company cars
Taxation of company cars: the appropriate percentage for 2028 to 2029 and 2029 to 2030
Rates and thresholds for employers 2026 to 2027

dieselExample.quote: Example 4 – diesel car Price of the car is £15,000. Approved figure of CO2 emissions is 156g/km. Round down 156 to 155 Look up appropriate percentage in Appendix 2 – 32%. Add 4% diesel supplement ( see chapter 12 paragraph 12.29 ), so appropriate percentage is 36%. The figure at step 5 is £15,000 x 36% = £5,400.

rde2.quote: from April 2018 if the diesel car is certified to meet Euro standard 6d it’s exempt from the supplement

capital.quote: the total of the capital sums contributed by the employee in that, and any earlier years, to expenditure on the provision of the car or any qualifying accessory taken into account at Step 2 £5,000

unavailable.quote: When the car is unavailable for any part of the year, the figure carried forward from Step 5 is reduced in proportion to the number of days of unavailability.

unavailableMeaning.quote: A car is treated as being ‘unavailable’ on any day if the day falls: (a) Before the first day on which the car is available to the employee. (b) After the last day on which the car is available to the employee. (c) Within a period of 30 or more consecutive days throughout which the car is not available to the employee.

privateUse.quote: Payments that an employee makes for the private use of the car are deducted from the figure carried forward from Step 6 and can reduce the benefit charge to nil.

fuel.quote: If your employer pays for fuel you use for personal journeys, you’ll pay tax on this separately.

phev.quote: The value of your car will be based on CO2 emissions of 1g/km if all of the following apply: it was registered on or after 1 January 2025 to 5 April 2028 it has CO2 emissions of 51g/km or more on the registration certificate it has an electric range of at least 1 mile the registration certificate does not show Euro 6d-ISC-FCM or Euro 6e in the ‘Euro status’ section

limit.quote: Section 141 ITEPA sets out the rules for diesel cars. Section 141(2) will be amended to reflect the 1 percentage point increases in appropriate percentage limit for tax years 2028 to 2029 and 2029 to 2030.

future.quote: Vehicles with CO2 emissions of 1g to 50g per kilometre will have appropriate percentages of 18% in 2028 to 2029 and 19% 2029 to 2030.

future2.quote: the appropriate percentage used to calculate an individual’s company car tax for zero emission vehicles will increase for 2028 to 2029 and 2029 to 2030 by 2 percentage points per year.

class1a.quote: The National Insurance Class 1A rate on expenses and benefits for 2026 to 2027 is 15%.

listPrice.quote: It includes standard accessories, any relevant taxes (VAT, car tax (where appropriate), any customs or excise duty, any tax chargeable as if it were a customs duty) and delivery charges, but excludes the new car registration fee because it’s an administration fee, not a tax. The list price is not the dealer’s advertised price for the car, nor the price paid for the car, which may incorporate discounts or cashbacks from the list price. Second-hand cars are treated in exactly the same way as new cars.

taxCode.quote: If a change affects the value of the car, HMRC will update your tax code so you pay the right tax.
